newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says it will stop Regent off-shore fund.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says it will stop Regent off-shore fund.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom on Monday said it had written to Regent Fund requiring it to stop an off-shore fund that intends to invest in domestic Gazprom shares.

"RAO Gazprom intends to take all necessary steps to prevent the realisation of Regent Fund's plan and other similar schemes regarding the shares of the company," Gazprom said of the plan by Regent Gaz Investment Company Limited.

"RAO Gazprom believes that the substance of Regent Fund's actions is contrary to normative acts of the Russian Federation providing for national security while giving foreign capital access to the Russian economy," it said in a statement.

Gazprom did not specify what steps it would take to stop Regent Gaz, based in the Cayman Islands. Gazprom had said Regent intended to create a $200 million fund backed by domestic Gazprom shares bought by a Regent subsidiary in Russia.
Gazprom said the fund was also contrary to its charter.

"These normative acts constitute the foundation for the restrictions in RAO Gazprom's Charter on foreign shareholdings in RAO Gazprom. Gazprom is discussing this issue with the Government of the Russian Federation," it said.
Gazprom in October 1996 launched an American Depositary Share (ADS) which allows international trading in Gazprom but trades at a price about four times that of underlying shares traded in Russia.

The premium is based largely on the difficulty of buying and trading local shares in the world's largest natural gas company and a number of equity analysts and traders have said the price of Gazprom's ADSs would be hurt by the plan.

The Regent Gaz fund would be managed by Regent Fund Management in Hong Kong, part of the Regent Pacific Group, a spokesman for the group said. Regent European Securities, a Moscow broker, is also a group subsidiary, the spokesman.
Gazprom ADSs in London were trading at 1150 GMT at $18.1500, up from $17.1250 at Friday's close.
